source: PlagaNet: Offline AI Pest Diagnosis for Peruvian Potato and Corn Farmers
one_liner: PlagaNet gives Peruvian potato and corn farmers instant, offline pest diagnosis from a photo, reducing crop loss from misdiagnosis and delayed expert visits.
problem: Peruvian potato and corn smallholders (~1.5M households) suffer 20-40% yield loss annually from pests and diseases, worth $500M+ in lost income. Current workarounds are guessing, asking neighbors, or waiting days for an agronomist, leading to over- or under-spraying and resistant pests. Evidence: INEI confirms 70% of rural farming families own smartphones, but internet connectivity is unreliable in major growing regions (Huancavelica, Apurimac, Cusco).
solution_insight: A mobile app that uses on-device computer vision trained on locally sourced images of 15+ common pests/diseases. Farmers take a photo and get actionable recommendations in Spanish and Quechua, offline. The non-obvious insight: farmers trust photos more than verbal descriptions, and offline-first eliminates connectivity barriers, while anonymized aggregated data can be sold to Agrorural for pest outbreak monitoring, creating a B2G revenue stream that subsidizes farmer freemium.
why_now: Smartphone penetration in rural Peru passed 70% in 2024 (INEI MICS); on-device ML inference (TensorFlow Lite) is mature; MINAGRI's 'Agricultura Digital 2025' policy mandates tech adoption; widespread pesticide misuse creates urgency for accurate, low-cost diagnosis.

market.recommended_focus: Peru: local pest relevance, pre-existing government interest via Agrorural, and first-mover data moat, though standalone market is sub-scale.

regions.validity: Peru is the natural starting market due to domestic pest species, farmer demographics, and potential B2G partnership with Agrorural. However, the TAM is below venture-scale thresholds; scaling within LATAM or adding crops is necessary.
regions.tam_topdown: MINAGRI estimates the Peruvian crop protection market for potato and corn at $380M (2023). If AI diagnosis captures 5% of that market as efficiency gains, TAM ~$19M. A more direct estimate from AgTech adoption rates suggests 10% of the 1.5M farmers paying $10/mo = $180M (BCRP survey on rural fintech adoption yields similar ARPU).
regions.tam_bottomup: 1.5M potato/corn farming households × $120/year ARPU (freemium conversion to premium + B2G) = $180M. Validate: $180M aligns with top-down.
regions.tam_consensus: $180M, but venture-scale ARR potential below $50M in Peru alone. Sub-venture-scale without international expansion or multi-crop strategy.
regions.sam: 30% of TAM = $54M (farmers with at least intermittent connectivity and smartphones; MTPE rural employment data supports smartphone ownership).
regions.som_12_months: 5,000 freemium users × 5% conversion × $60/year = $15,000 + B2G pilot with Agrorural @ $50,000 = $65,000 ARR.

regions.validity: Similar Andean crops (Ecuador, Bolivia, Colombia) add ~2M farmers, but language and pest variance require additional data collection. TAM ~$400M, still borderline venture scale.
regions.tam_topdown: FAO report on Andean crop protection market ~$800M, 20% addressable by AI diagnosis = $160M; adjusted for farmer income: ~$400M.

regions.validity: Large corn and potato industries but different pests, high connectivity, and sophisticated agribusiness; offline AI adds little value. Not an initial target.
regions.tam_bottomup: 10,000 large potato/corn farms × $5,000/year = $50M. Mismatch; top-down likely overestimates AI diagnostics share.

source_strategy: TAM bottom-up: number of farmers from INEI agricultural census 2012, adjusted for annual growth; ARPU from BCRP rural income surveys and comparable AgTech freemium conversion benchmarks.
SAM: filter farmers by smartphone ownership (INEI household surveys) and pest prevalence regions (SENASA reports).
SOM: direct sales funnel estimate: 5,000 downloads via WhatsApp campaigns and cooperative partnerships, 5% monthly active premium conversion.

competition_moat.moat_advantage: Farmers lose 20-40% yield; PlagaNet provides instant, science-backed decisions, reducing waste.

competition_moat.competitor: Manual agronomist visits ($20-50/visit, days of delay)
competition_moat.moat_advantage: Zero marginal cost, offline, 24/7; agronomists can handle more strategic tasks.

competition_moat.competitor: Plantix / generic AI apps (online, not trained on Peruvian pests)
competition_moat.moat_advantage: Offline-first, local pest model (e.g., Andean weevil, late blight races), Quechua support, B2G integration.

business_model_pricing.freemium: Free: 5 diagnoses/month, basic alert; ads for government recommendations.
business_model_pricing.premium: $5/month: unlimited diagnoses, pest lifecycle tracking, personalized spray alerts.
business_model_pricing.b2g: $2/farmer/month to Agrorural for aggregated pest surveillance dashboard + early-warning system, with volume discounts after 1,000 farmers.
business_model_pricing.contribution_margin: ~90% after initial model training; variable cost is negligible cloud sync (offline core) and support.

go_to_market.first_10_users: Pilot with 10 farmers from a cooperative in Huancayo (potato) via direct demonstration at a community meeting, using a 3G tablet to prove offline utility.
go_to_market.first_100_users: Recruit via 5 Agrorural extension officers in Cusco and Apurimac who already have farmer trust; offer free premium for 3 months in exchange for pest photo submissions.
go_to_market.first_1000_users: WhatsApp broadcast to 50 farmer groups, agricultural radio spots in Quechua, and presence at regional fairs (Ferias Agropecuarias).
go_to_market.b2g_entry: Pilot with Agrorural's national pest monitoring network: deploy to 50 officers, demonstrate 30% faster outbreak detection.

traction_signals.interviews: 30 farmer interviews across 4 regions: 80% willing to try if free, 40% would pay $5/month if accurate (verbally).
traction_signals.waitlist: 45 farmers signed up via WhatsApp after seeing a demo video.
traction_signals.lois: Letter of Interest from President of Junín Potato Growers Association, expressing intent to pilot with 200 members.
traction_signals.data: Amassed 2,500 labeled images from INIA (Instituto Nacional de Innovación Agraria) public database and farmer-sourced photos.

roadmap.month_1: Collect 1,000 additional labeled images from field visits in Junín; train baseline model (late blight, Andean weevil, fall armyworm). Onboard 10 beta farmers on WhatsApp. No revenue.
roadmap.month_2: Launch MVP with offline classification on cheap Android devices. Test with 30 farmers, achieve >80% accuracy in field conditions. Target 5 paid beta users.
roadmap.month_3: Integrate Quechua voice feedback. Start Agrorural pilot with 5 extensionists. Goal: 50 free users, 10 paid.
roadmap.month_6: 500 free users, 20 paid (MRR $100). Agrorural pilot expands to 20 officers, B2G revenue $10,000 (3-month pilot contract). Key metric: user-retention >30% at day 30.
roadmap.month_9: 2,000 free users, 100 paid (MRR $500). B2G quarterly budget allocated by MINAGRI. CAC target: $3 via WhatsApp referrals.
roadmap.month_12: 5,000 free users, 250 paying (MRR $1,250). B2G annual contract of $50,000 with Agrorural for district-level monitoring. Total ARR $65,000.

risks_mitigations.mitigation: Confidence threshold (<70% -> recommend visiting agronomist); continuous model improvement via user uploads; incentivize field photos with geo-tagging.
Design for LATAM expansion (Ecuador, Bolivia) and multi-crop (quinoa, coffee) from day one; B2G component targets a $200M LATAM AgTech government market.
Pilot with Agrorural via research grant (PNIA); use LOIs to demonstrate demand; maintain direct-to-farmer channel to reduce dependency.
Partner with local cooperatives and trusted agronomists; include simple visual outputs and audio in Quechua; field demos.

budget_breakdown.line: Field data collection (travel, farmer incentives, labeling)
budget_breakdown.rationale: Critical for building a local dataset that no generic model has; 20 trips to 4 regions, $2,000/trip.

budget_breakdown.line: ML engineering (2 part-time researchers for 6 months)
budget_breakdown.rationale: Need expertise in on-device optimization and pest domain; not a full stack hire.

budget_breakdown.line: MVP app development (React Native + TensorFlow Lite)
budget_breakdown.rationale: Basic offline diagnosis UI, subscription integration, and dashboard for Agrorural.
Cost of onboarding 200 farmers and 10 extensionists, travel, and legal for pilot contract with Agrorural.
Incorporate in Peru, SAE registration, privacy policy for B2G data sharing.

the_ask.milestone_unlocked: 20 paying farmers (MRR $100) and 1 signed B2G pilot contract with Agrorural, proving willingness to pay on both sides.
the_ask.critical_assumption_being_tested: Peruvian smallholders will pay $5/month for an AI diagnosis app and that Agrorural will pay for aggregated data.
the_ask.why_not_less: $50k would only fund app development without the data collection needed to reach minimum viable accuracy, killing the core value prop.
the_ask.why_not_more: $500k would be premature; the team has not proven field accuracy or sales cycles; after 12 months, a seed round based on traction can be raised.

product_demo_architecture.mobile_app: Android/iOS built with React Native; offline TensorFlow Lite model (MobileNetV3-based, quantized) for 8 pest/disease classes; on-device recommendation database in Spanish/Quechua; optional sync when online to backend.
product_demo_architecture.backend: Node.js on AWS Lambda for premium account management, aggregated anonymized data for B2G dashboard (React web app for MINAGRI), and model update distribution.
product_demo_architecture.data_pipeline: Scripts in Python to augment INIA dataset with synthetic lighting variations; active learning loop from consented photos.
product_demo_architecture.offline_model_performance: Target inference <2 seconds on a $100 Android device, accuracy >85% top-1 on in-distribution test set.

rating: NO-GO — High market risk, untested team, insufficient traction, but concept addresses real pain and could become venture-scale with LATAM expansion and B2G lock-in.
external_research_hooks: INEI - Encuesta Nacional de Hogares 2023: 72% de hogares rurales con al menos un smartphone y 39% con acceso a internet móvil en zonas altoandinas.
MINAGRI - Estrategia Nacional de Agricultura Digital 2025: prioriza alertas tempranas de plagas usando TIC.
SENASA - Reporte de brotes de tizón tardío 2023: 18% de área de papa afectada en Huánuco.
BCRP - Encuesta de Ingresos de Hogares Rurales 2022: ingreso promedio mensual de productores de papa es S/ 890, dispuestos a gastar 0.6% en insumos de información.
MTPE - Perfil del Productor Agropecuario 2021: 58% de agricultores de papa y maíz tienen primaria incompleta; el 80% prefiere información en quechua.

fatal_flaws.risk: Total addressable market in Peru is below $50M ARR, making it impossible to achieve venture-scale returns without massive international expansion or a radical pricing model change.
fatal_flaws.why_it_matters: VCs need companies that can reach $1B+ valuations; a $180M TAM with 5% penetration yields $9M revenue, not enough.
fatal_flaws.fast_test: Interview 10 LATAM agtech VCs about required market size and expansion timelines; research if any $1B exits exist in smallholder agtech.

fatal_flaws.risk: Misdiagnosis rate on low-cost phones in poor lighting may exceed 30%, causing farmers to abandon the app and return to guesswork, destroying reputation.
fatal_flaws.why_it_matters: One wrong recommendation leading to crop failure can permanently blacklist the product in a community.
fatal_flaws.fast_test: Take 100 field photos with a $50 Android in typical midday light, use existing Plantix API (if available) to estimate baseline accuracy; if below 70%, the offline model won't work without major data investment.

fatal_flaws.risk: Government procurement cycle is unpredictable and may never materialize; Agrorural budget codes are not pre-allocated for AI surveillance.
fatal_flaws.why_it_matters: The B2G revenue line is critical for sustainability; without it, the unit economics from farmers alone are unsustainable (CAC > LTV).
fatal_flaws.fast_test: FOIA request or direct inquiry to MINAGRI's OSCE registry to find if any SaaS pest monitoring contract has been issued in the last 3 years; talk to 3 former Agrorural procurement officers.

first_10_customers.action: Visit the Junín Potato Growers Association monthly meeting, provide a live demo on 5 fields, and onboard the president and 4 lead farmers via WhatsApp group.
first_10_customers.target_persona: Smallholder potato farmers (>2 ha) in Huancayo, cooperative leaders
first_10_customers.how_to_reach: Contact association secretary via known INIA referral, bring a tablet with pre-loaded demo, and offer a 6-month free premium for early sign-ups.

first_10_customers.action: Piggyback on a SENASA training workshop on pest management in Cusco; set up a booth and offer instant diagnosis for farmers bringing infested leaves.
first_10_customers.target_persona: Corn and potato farmers attending government training
first_10_customers.how_to_reach: Coordinate with SENASA regional office; prepare laminated cards with sample images and QR code to download app; collect 30+ contacts.

first_10_customers.action: Cold-call two agronomists working for Agrorural in Apurimac, offer them a private dashboard to monitor their assigned farmers, and ask them to recruit 5 trusted farmers each.
first_10_customers.how_to_reach: Source names from MINAGRI regional directory; message: 'We have a tool that can save you two hours of field diagnosis per week; can we show you via video call?'

mvp_2_week_test.build: A single-screen React Web App (mobile-optimized) with a file upload button. Backend runs a Python FastAPI server with a pre-trained YOLOv8n model fine-tuned on 500 public images of potato late blight and corn fall armyworm. When a photo is uploaded, it returns the pest name and confidence. No user accounts or offline capability.
mvp_2_week_test.cut: No native app, no offline, no B2G dashboard, no multi-class classification, no payment system, no localization.
mvp_2_week_test.test_hypothesis: If we show this to 10 farmers and 3 extensionists in Huancayo and at least 5 farmers say they would use it weekly and would pay S/ 10/month (via informal commitment), then the core value prop is validated.
mvp_2_week_test.success_signal: >50% of demo participants agree to a follow-up WhatsApp group and express willingness to pay verbally or sign a non-binding LOI.
